novel.justification: Potential-mean continuity is a genuine untestable but mild continuous-dose causal regularity condition. It is satisfied when mean biological response varies continuously with dose within each recorded stratum, including the smooth Legendre--Bernoulli hard family. It is not implied by Sobolev smoothness of the observed signed channel \(q_x\), does not aid analytic recovery, and does not determine the band rate.

novel.justification:
For each fixed error law, continuity of its characteristic function together with \(\phi_r(0)=1\) implies a distribution-specific neighborhood and a distribution-specific positive lower modulus. Requiring the same declared \(
u\) and \(c_{\phi}\) for every law in \(\mathcal M\) is instead a maintained quantitative uniform-strength restriction. It is satisfied by scientifically calibrated families of recall-error laws whose low-frequency characteristic functions vary in a compact neighborhood of a reference family, and it still permits open spectral zero sets outside \([-
u,
u]\). The restriction neither encodes identification, coverage, diameter, nor the minimax rate, and no published comparator is claimed as its source.

This lower-envelope restriction is a new quantitative adaptation index, not a standard deconvolution assumption. In the restricted family \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(\gamma\) measures worst-case polynomial attenuation of both recall-error transforms and \(L\) measures their usable frequency scale. The class describes replicate instruments whose characteristic functions remain uniformly informative through expanding frequency windows; its polynomial members can be compared with the lower-modulus side of ordinary-smooth error models, while the unrestricted fixed class \(\mathcal M\) still permits open spectral zeros.

This is response regularity for the primitive signed first-moment density \(q_x(a)\,da=E_P[Y\,1\{A\in da\}\mid X=x]\), not a property borrowed from density deconvolution. A concrete sufficient primitive subclass has \(f_x\) and a bounded \(H^{\beta}(\mathbb R)\) extension of \(a\mapsto E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) in fixed Sobolev balls. Since \(H^{\beta}(\mathbb R)\) is a multiplication algebra for \(\beta>1/2\), their product \(q_x\) has \(H^{\beta}\) norm bounded by \(C_{\beta}\) times the product of those two fixed radii; smooth bounded Bernoulli response probabilities on compact dose support give such laws.

definitions.name: Fixed blind-replicate ADRF class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P: P\text{ obeys finite-stratum positivity, causal consistency, weak unconfoundedness, continuity on }\mathcal I\text{ of each potential-mean curve }m_x^{\mathrm{pot}},\text{ bounded potential outcomes, compact dose support, classical independent replicate errors with }E_P[U_1]=0\text{ and the stated first-error absolute-moment bound, the maintained quantitative local-modulus restriction with fixed common }\nu\text{ and }c_{\phi},\text{ the latent-density Sobolev bound, the novel outcome-weighted response-regularity bound, and target-interval positivity}\}\), with the fixed constants satisfying the necessary nonemptiness coherence \(|\mathcal X_0|p_{\min}\le1\).

definitions.name: Continuous Sobolev representative convention
definitions.construction: For each \(x\in\mathcal X_0\), \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) are defined to be the unique continuous \(H^{\beta}(\mathbb R)\) functions equal almost everywhere to, respectively, the conditional-density class \(dP(A\le a\mid X=x)/da\) and the observed signed-density class \(E_P[Y1\{A\in da\}\mid X=x]/da\). Under the potential-mean continuity condition, the separately declared \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]\) denotes a fixed continuous version on \(\mathcal I\); no equality between \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}\) and the observed canonical ratio \(\mu_x=q_x/f_x\) is part of this convention. Pointwise values of \(\mu_x(a)\), \(\mu(a)\), \(\mu_{\vartheta}(a)\), \(L_n(a)\), and \(U_n(a)\), as well as every \(\|\cdot\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}\) separation, use these declared versions and representatives.

definitions.name: Coupled transform factorization
definitions.construction: For every \(x\in\mathcal X_0\), \(F_x(s,t)=\mathcal Ff_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\) and \(G_x(s,t)=\mathcal Fq_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\).

definitions.name: Constrained joint analytic sieve
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_m\) is the set of tuples \(\vartheta=(p_{\vartheta},\{f_{\vartheta x},q_{\vartheta x}\}_{x\in\mathcal X_0},Q_{\vartheta1},Q_{\vartheta2})\) satisfying the simplex and \(p_{\vartheta x}\ge p_{\min}\) restrictions, support, first-error centering, normalization, density-positivity, outcome-domination, the first-absolute-moment bound for the first error, the maintained quantitative local-modulus restriction with the fixed common \(\nu\) and \(c_{\phi}\), latent-density Sobolev, and outcome-weighted response-regularity constraints of \(\mathcal M\), with observable restrictions evaluated through \(T_mf_{\vartheta x}\) and \(T_mq_{\vartheta x}\); their deterministic transform-approximation allowance is \(d_m\).

definitions.name: Coupled empirical-characteristic-function confidence set
definitions.construction: Every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) must satisfy \(p_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_n(\alpha)\). If \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X_0}n_x<2\), this multinomial restriction is the only empirical restriction and \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)=\{\vartheta\in\Theta_{m_n}:p_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_n(\alpha)\}\). Otherwise, \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) additionally requires, simultaneously over \(x\in\mathcal X_0\), \((s,t)\in\Gamma_n\), \(j\in\{F,G\}\), and \(b\in\{R,I\}\), except the deterministic \(F\)-channel coordinates at \((s,t)=(0,0)\), that the residual \(\widehat j_x(s,t)-T_{m_n}h_{\vartheta jx}(s+t)\phi_{\vartheta1}(s)\phi_{\vartheta2}(t)\) obeys \(|\operatorname{part}_b(\mathrm{residual})|\le R_{n,jxb}(s,t)+d_{m_n}\), where \(h_{\vartheta Fx}=f_{\vartheta x}\) and \(h_{\vartheta Gx}=q_{\vartheta x}\). A coordinate with zero empirical variance is retained with radius \(8c_{n,\alpha}^{2}/(n_x-1)+d_{m_n}\), rather than divided by zero or silently dropped.

definitions.name: Projected ADRF band
definitions.construction: If \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X_0}n_x\ge2\), then for \(a\in\mathcal I\), set \(L_n(a)=\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_0}p_{\vartheta x}q_{\vartheta x}(a)/f_{\vartheta x}(a)\) and \(U_n(a)=\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_0}p_{\vartheta x}q_{\vartheta x}(a)/f_{\vartheta x}(a)\), projecting the candidate observed canonical ratios and evaluating every candidate \(f_{\vartheta x}\) and \(q_{\vartheta x}\) at its unique continuous \(H^{\beta}\) representative. If \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)=\varnothing\) or some \(n_x<2\), set \([L_n(a),U_n(a)]=[-1,1]\) for every \(a\in\mathcal I\).

definitions.name: All-strata fixed-marginal Legendre--Bernoulli hard family
definitions.construction: Let \(h(u)=c_h\{\sin(u)/u\}^{12}\), where \(c_h\) normalizes the integral, and let \(h_{\eta}(u)=h(u)\{1+\eta\sin(u/4)\}\). Fix distinct \(\eta_1,\eta_2\in(0,1/4)\), set \(d_{\eta_1}=\int uh_{\eta_1}(u)du\), let \(Q_1^{\star}\) have density \(u\mapsto h_{\eta_1}(u+d_{\eta_1})\), and let \(Q_2^{\star}\) have density \(h_{\eta_2}\); thus only the first error is normalized to have mean zero. Write \(\phi_r^{\star}(t)=E_{Q_r^{\star}}[e^{itU_r}]\). The fixed quantitative class is calibrated to these witnesses with strict slack so that \(E_{Q_1^{\star}}|U_1|<M_U\) and the maintained common-strength condition \(\min_{r\in\{1,2\}}\inf_{|t|\le\nu}|\phi_r^{\star}(t)|>c_{\phi}\) holds, while both transforms have compact support. Take the declared \(f_0\), whose fixed-class calibration gives \(\inf_{a\in\mathcal I}f_0(a)>\kappa\) and \(\|f_0\|_{H^{\beta}}<H_0\). Choose an affine copy \(J\) of \([-1,1]\) strictly inside \(\mathcal I\), set \(\rho_m(z)=m\rho(mz)\), and choose a fixed \(c_v>0\) small enough that, for all sufficiently large \(m\), \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal I}|v_m(a)/f_0(a)|\le1/4\) and \(\|f_0/2+v_m\|_{H^{\beta}}\vee\|f_0/2-v_m\|_{H^{\beta}}<H_0\). On \(J\), set \(v_m(a)=c_v m^{1/2-\beta}\{(P_m1_{[-1,1]})*\rho_m\}\) after the affine change of variables, and set it to zero off the mollified copy of \(J\). Draw \(X\sim p^{\star}\), and conditionally on every \(X=x\) draw \(A\sim f_0\). Draw \((U_1,U_2)\sim Q_1^{\star}\otimes Q_2^{\star}\) and \(V\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)\) mutually independently and independently of \((X,A)\). For each sign and every stratum, define the identical potential-outcome process \(Y_{m,\pm}(a)=1\{V\le1/2\pm v_m(a)/f_0(a)\}\), so \(m_{x,\pm}^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1/2\pm v_m(a)/f_0(a)\), and observe \(Y=Y_{m,\pm}(A)\).

definitions.name: All-strata homogeneous fixed-marginal Bernoulli subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\star}=\{P_g\in\mathcal M:P_g(X=x)=p_x^{\star},\ f_x=f_0,\mathcal L_{P_g}(U_1,U_2)=Q_1^{\star}\otimes Q_2^{\star},\mathcal L_{P_g}(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+g(a)/f_0(a))\text{ for }f_0(a)>0,\ q_x=f_0/2+g,\text{ and }m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}=1/2+g/f_0\text{ on }\mathcal I\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X_0,\text{ where the common }g\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathcal I^{\circ})\text{ obeys }\sup_{a\in\mathcal I}|g(a)/f_0(a)|\le1/4\text{ and }\|f_0/2+g\|_{H^{\beta}}\le H_0\}\).

definitions.name: Nested operator-strength subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(\lambda)=\{P\in\mathcal M:\underline\varphi_P(T)\ge\lambda(T)\text{ for every }T\ge\nu\}\) for \(\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}\). If \(\lambda_1(T)\le\lambda_2(T)\) for every \(T\), then \(\mathcal M(\lambda_2)\subseteq\mathcal M(\lambda_1)\). Polynomial ordinary-smooth error models satisfying a two-sided transform bound of order \((1+T)^{-\gamma}\) lie in a corresponding member whenever its lower constant dominates \(L\).

definitions.name: Empirical spectral-envelope adaptation handle
definitions.construction: For a nested grid in the polynomial-attenuation family \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}\), form simultaneous empirical lower confidence envelopes for \(|\phi_1(t)|\) and \(|\phi_2(t)|\), retain the largest frequency square on which the lower envelope dominates \(\lambda_{\gamma,L}\), invert the corresponding confidence set, and select the smallest projected band whose intersections with every coarser \(\mathcal M(\lambda_{\gamma,L})\) confidence set are nonempty. Calibrate the tests against the deceptive-pair functional \(\Delta_n(\lambda,w)\) and candidate frontier \(s_n^{\star}(\lambda)\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X_0\), let \(\delta=\min\{\nu,(4R)^{-1}\}\). Compact support implies \(|\mathcal Ff_x(u)|\ge1-R|u|\ge3/4\) for \(|u|\le\delta\); hence \(|F_x(s,t)|\ge3c_{\phi}^2/4\) whenever \(|s|,|t|,|s+t|\le\delta\). If two laws \(P,P^{\prime}\in\mathcal M\) have the same observed law and the treatment-channel cocycle has established equality of their \(L^1\)-classes for \(f_x\) and of their two error transforms, then the local observable ratio \(\mathcal Fq_x(s+t)=\mathcal Ff_x(s+t)G_x(s,t)/F_x(s,t)\) establishes equality of \(\mathcal Fq_x\) on \([-\delta,\delta]\). Because \(q_x(a)da\) is a compactly supported finite signed measure, its Fourier transform is entire, so analytic continuation gives equality of the global \(L^1\)- and \(L^2\)-equivalence classes; the continuous-representative convention then gives pointwise equality of \(q_x\). Finally, for any two admissible pairs on \(\mathcal I\), \(f_x,f_x^{\prime}\ge\kappa\) and \(|q_x^{\prime}|\le f_x^{\prime}\) give \[\left\|\frac{q_x}{f_x}-\frac{q_x^{\prime}}{f_x^{\prime}}\right\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}\le\kappa^{-1}\bigl(\|q_x-q_x^{\prime}\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}+\|f_x-f_x^{\prime}\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}\bigr),\] so recovery and continuation of the signed numerator precede stable division for the observed canonical ratio. Its pointwise equality to the potential-mean curve is a separate causal step in the identification theorem.
statements.justification: The shared signed channel requires its own local ratio, signed-measure continuation, and stable division argument; it is not an automatic corollary of latent-density identification.
statements.gap: LiVuong1998, Lemma 2.1 and equations (1)--(2) on pp. 140--142, identifies latent and error densities from two indicators under globally nonvanishing characteristic functions, while Schennach2004, Theorem 1 and equations (11)--(16) on pp. 1049--1051, already identifies a regression numerator and denominator from repeated measurements under a globally nonvanishing observed transform. CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 identifies a positive latent law and the error laws when zeros are permitted. None gives the local observable ratio, compactly supported signed-measure continuation, and denominator-stable causal ratio transfer stated here for open zero sets.
statements.consumer: The transfer lemma makes numerator recovery auditable before the causal equality and projected-band arguments control the nonlinear ratio.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the observed law of \(O=(Y,X,S_1,S_2)\) uniquely determines \(p_x\), the \(L^1\)- and \(L^2\)-equivalence classes of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\), their declared unique continuous \(H^{\beta}(\mathbb R)\) representatives, and \(\phi_1\) and \(\phi_2\). Specifically, the treatment transforms obey the multiplicative cocycle on \([-\nu,\nu]^2\); the finite first absolute moment of \(U_1\) justifies the derivative-at-zero location step, and \(E_P[U_1]=0\) alone removes the common translation indeterminacy. The signed-channel transfer lemma then uses the local observable \(G_x/F_x\) ratio, analytic continuation of the compactly supported signed measure \(q_x(a)da\), and denominator stability before division. Consistency and weak unconfoundedness imply \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) for \(P_{A\mid X=x}\)-almost every \(a\in\mathcal I\), hence \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=q_x(a)/f_x(a)\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in\mathcal I\) because \(f_x\ge\kappa\). Continuity of the separately maintained potential-mean version \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}\) and of the canonical Sobolev ratio \(q_x/f_x\) promotes this equality to every \(a\in\mathcal I\). Consequently, the causal target \(\mu(a)=E_P[Y(a)]=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_0}p_xm_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_0}p_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\) is identified pointwise on \(\mathcal I\). On the compact-support submodel of the broader H2 exponential-moment/tail class treated by CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025, this result adds identification of a shared signed outcome channel and its equality to the causal ADRF under the stated causal conditions; it does not enlarge their latent-law class.
statements.justification: This root identification contribution recovers the signed numerator through open spectral gaps before division; the already-known nonvanishing repeated-measurement regression machinery is not counted as new.
statements.gap: Unknown-error repeated-measurement identification, replicate-based error-law recovery, and regression numerator--denominator deconvolution are already established by LiVuong1998, Lemma 2.1 and equations (1)--(8) on pp. 140--143, and Schennach2004, Theorem 1 and equations (11)--(16) on pp. 1049--1051, under their nonvanishing regimes. CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 identifies the positive latent law and errors over a broader H2 exponential-moment/tail class. The new claim is confined to joint analytic recovery of the compact-support latent density and shared signed channel when the two unknown error transforms are nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have open zero sets, followed by the explicit pointwise causal continuity bridge; it does not claim those foundational repeated-measurement operations as novel.
statements.consumer: This gives a nonparametric identification foundation for two-recall diet--mortality dose-response analyses in which recall errors are asymmetric and their spectra may contain intervals of zeros.

statements.statement: There is a choice of \(c_m>0\) and constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on the fixed radii of \(\mathcal M\), such that with \(m_n=\lfloor c_m\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), probability at least \(1-o(1)\) uniformly in \(P\in\mathcal M\), one has \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X_0}n_x\ge2\), \(p\in\mathcal P_n(\alpha)\), and every two elements \(\vartheta,\vartheta^{\prime}\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) satisfy \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal I}|\mu_{\vartheta}(a)-\mu_{\vartheta^{\prime}}(a)|\le C\{r_n+|\mathcal X_0|\epsilon_{n,\alpha}\}\le Cr_n\), where every pointwise value and supremum uses the declared unique continuous Sobolev representatives. The \(|\mathcal X_0|\epsilon_{n,\alpha}=O(n^{-1/2})\) term is the contribution of jointly projecting the stratum-mass vector. The proof must derive the inverse modulus from the local coupled transform residuals with the total empirical-Bernstein radii, compact-support Taylor continuation, the \(H^{\beta}\)-to-\(L^{\infty}\) tail inequality, and the stable representative-based ratio under \(f_x\ge\kappa\); it may not assume this diameter as a primitive condition.
statements.justification: This is the quantitative bridge from qualitative analytic identification to a shrinking causal confidence band.
statements.gap: LiVuong1998, Theorems 3.1--3.4 on pp. 147--151, derives uniform density-estimation rates for four ordinary- and supersmooth nonvanishing cases; Schennach2004, Theorem 2 on pp. 1059--1061, derives pointwise regression rates from Fourier numerator--denominator recovery; and DelaigleHallMeister2008, Theorems 3.1 and 3.5 on pp. 670--676, gives first-order equivalence to known-error point estimators. CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 controls latent-density \(L^2\) risk, and KatoSasakiUra2021 proves fixed-alternative power. None derives the coupled open-zero ADRF sup-norm confidence-set diameter needed for an honest simultaneous band.
statements.consumer: The diameter result supplies a rate-calibrated uncertainty envelope rather than a merely consistent identified set for the NHANES two-recall response curve.

statements.statement: Use the declared defaults \(\widehat F_x=1\{(s,t)=(0,0)\}\), \(\widehat G_x=0\), and zero empirical scales when \(n_x=0\); use the full band \([-1,1]\) when any \(n_x<2\) or the confidence set is empty. Jointly invert \(p\) through \(\mathcal P_n(\alpha)\), project each candidate observed canonical ratio using \(p_{\vartheta}\) and the candidate continuous Sobolev representatives, allocate noncoverage \(\alpha/2\) to the simultaneous multinomial region, and allocate \(\alpha/2\) to the transform restrictions. Calibrate \(c_{n,\alpha}\) over the positive-variance coordinate set \(\mathcal D_n\), excluding the deterministic \(F_x(0,0)\) coordinates, and use \(R_{n,jxb}(s,t)\) on every retained confidence-set coordinate, including its additive convention when empirical variance is zero. Under consistency, weak unconfoundedness, target positivity, and potential-mean continuity, the identification theorem gives \(\mu_P(a)=\sum_xp_xm_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=\sum_xp_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\) pointwise on \(\mathcal I\). Therefore \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P\{\mu_P(a)\in[L_n(a),U_n(a)]\ \forall a\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_P[W(\mathcal B_n)]\le C\{r_n+|\mathcal X_0|\epsilon_{n,\alpha}\}\le Cr_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Potential-mean continuity is used only to certify the pointwise causal interpretation; it does not enter analytic recovery or the diameter bound. The root-\(n\) multinomial term is negligible relative to the logarithmic continuation rate, and the exponentially small event \(\min_x n_x<2\) is included in both assertions through the full-band default.
statements.justification: This root inference contribution supplies uniform simultaneous coverage and quantitative worst-case width in the open-zero blind model; unknown-error regression point estimation itself is not counted as new.
statements.gap: LiVuong1998, equations (5)--(8) and Theorems 3.1--3.4 on pp. 142--151, already estimates unknown latent and error densities from repeated measurements; Schennach2004, Theorems 1--3 on pp. 1049--1063, already identifies and estimates a nonparametric regression numerator and denominator and derives pointwise rates and asymptotic normality; and DelaigleHallMeister2008, equations (2.1)--(2.6), condition (2.2), and Theorems 3.1 and 3.5 on pp. 668--676, already gives unknown-error repeated-measurement density and regression estimators and first-order equivalence to known-error estimators. Those operations are explicitly non-novel. Their operative global nonvanishing or common real-valued nowhere-zero regimes do not cover the jointly inverted causal ADRF band under blind nonidentical asymmetric errors with open spectral zero sets, and none proves a uniformly honest simultaneous causal band or an all-honest expected-width converse.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can report a simultaneous uncertainty band for the full dietary dose-response curve without specifying or externally estimating the recall-error distribution.

statements.statement: Assume the fixed-class constants satisfy the necessary coherence \(|\mathcal X_0|p_{\min}\le1\), and set \(p_x^{\star}=|\mathcal X_0|^{-1}\). The fixed witnesses can be selected with strict quantitative slack: \(\inf_{a\in\mathcal I}f_0(a)>\kappa\), \(\|f_0\|_{H^{\beta}}<H_0\), \(E_{Q_1^{\star}}|U_1|<M_U\), and \(\min_{r\in\{1,2\}}\inf_{|t|\le\nu}|\phi_r^{\star}(t)|>c_{\phi}\). A fixed sufficiently small \(c_v>0\) then gives, for both signs and all sufficiently large \(m\), \(\|f_0/2\pm v_m\|_{H^{\beta}}<H_0\) and \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal I}|v_m(a)/f_0(a)|\le1/4\). Consequently, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the all-strata Legendre--Bernoulli handle with \(m=m_n\) yields two laws \(P_{n,+},P_{n,-}\in\mathcal M_{\star}\). Under both laws, \(X\sim p^{\star}\); in every \(x\in\mathcal X_0\), \(A\mid X=x\sim f_0\); and the same two nonidentical asymmetric compact-spectrum error laws apply independently of \((X,A,Y(\cdot))\), with \(E[U_1]=0\). Thus the full law of \((X,S_1,S_2)\) is fixed across signs. In every stratum, \(q_{x,\pm}=f_0/2\pm v_{m_n}\) and the smooth potential-mean curves are identical across strata, \(m_{x,\pm}^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1/2\pm v_{m_n}(a)/f_0(a)\). Hence the maximum-over-strata latent and weighted Sobolev restrictions, target positivity, Bernoulli feasibility, potential-mean continuity, ignorability, consistency, and error exogeneity all hold. The marginal causal ADRFs satisfy \(\mu_{P_{n,\pm}}(a)=\sum_xp_x^{\star}m_{x,\pm}^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1/2\pm v_{m_n}(a)/f_0(a)\), so averaging over strata causes no attenuation and \(\|\mu_{P_{n,+}}-\mu_{P_{n,-}}\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}\ge c m_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp r_n\), with the separation evaluated through the declared versions and representatives. Writing \(R_{n,\pm}\) for the corresponding one-observation experiment after deleting \(X\), ancillary factorization gives \(P_{n,\pm,O}=p^{\star}\otimes R_{n,\pm}\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(P_{n,+,O}^{\otimes n},P_{n,-,O}^{\otimes n})=\operatorname{TV}(R_{n,+}^{\otimes n},R_{n,-}^{\otimes n})\le\rho\) for a fixed \(\rho<1-2\alpha\). These conclusions certify that the all-strata fixed-marginal subclass is nonempty and that the product-experiment contiguity calculation is unchanged by the ancillary stratum label.
statements.justification: The homogeneous all-strata construction isolates the outcome channel without changing the declared covariate support or attenuating the marginal ADRF separation.
statements.gap: CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 perturbs the latent density in \(L^2\), while LouniciNickl2011 perturbs a density under a known operator; neither maintains a fixed all-strata noisy-treatment marginal with Bernoulli outcomes and an ancillary covariate factor.
statements.consumer: The lemma determines whether outcome information can evade the severe analytic-continuation bottleneck; if it cannot, wider bands in nutritional applications are unavoidable rather than an artifact of the estimator.

statements.statement: For every sequence of random bands \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_n\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Hon}_{\alpha}(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_n,\mathcal M)\) for the causal target \(\mu_P(a)=\sum_xp_xm_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n^{-1}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\star}}E_P[W(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_n)]\ge c>0\). On the smooth all-strata Legendre--Bernoulli subclass, \(X\sim p^{\star}\) is ancillary, \(A\mid X=x\sim f_0\) and the error laws are common across all \(x\in\mathcal X_0\), potential-mean continuity holds, and the causal target equals the canonical observed ratio pointwise on \(\mathcal I\). Because the identical perturbation appears in every stratum, \(\sum_xp_x^{\star}m_{x,\pm}^{\mathrm{pot}}=m_{x,\pm}^{\mathrm{pot}}\) and there is no stratum attenuation. Thus the expected supremum width in the upper theorem is minimax-order optimal even on this all-strata fixed-\(f_0\), fixed-error Bernoulli subclass.
statements.justification: This root converse contribution uses the fixed-marginal outcome experiment and coverage-to-testing step to constrain every honest band, rather than relabelling an existing estimation-risk result.
statements.gap: Low1997 supplies the general testing inequality, but no published result provides the required outcome-channel alternatives or applies it to a blind-replicate ADRF band.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives practitioners a benchmark for judging whether an alternative two-recall band is genuinely more informative or has sacrificed uniform coverage.

statements.statement: On the fixed class \(\mathcal M\), the projected band \(\mathcal B_n\) is uniformly honest and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_P[W(\mathcal B_n)]\le Cr_n\). Conversely, every band sequence \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_n\) that is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal M\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n^{-1}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\star}}E_P[W(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_n)]\ge c>0\). Hence \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\) is the minimax order of expected supremum width for uniformly honest causal ADRF bands over the fixed class, already forced by the nonempty all-strata homogeneous fixed-treatment-marginal Bernoulli subclass with \(X\sim p^{\star}\) ancillary and no attenuation of the ADRF separation.
statements.justification: This shared root theorem records the exact fixed-class minimax consequence of the new upper band and all-honest lower bound without adding a fourth novelty claim.
statements.gap: LiVuong1998, Schennach2004, and DelaigleHallMeister2008 already establish unknown-error repeated-measurement density or regression point estimation in nonvanishing regimes, and Low1997 gives a generic confidence-length inequality. None establishes matching upper and all-honest expected-width bounds for a simultaneous causal ratio band under blind nonidentical open-zero replicates, particularly on a fixed noisy-treatment marginal with the homogeneous finite-stratum outcome hard family.
statements.consumer: The theorem provides one rate benchmark for evaluating the width of simultaneous two-recall ADRF bands in the NHANES application.

statements.statement: Already-known sanity benchmark, credited to HuangZhang2023 and excluded from the research theorem count: if the error characteristic function \(\phi_1\) is known and nonzero on \(\mathbb R\), then the observed functional reduces to \(\mathcal Fq_x(u)=G_x(u,0)/\phi_1(u)\), \(\mathcal Ff_x(u)=F_x(u,0)/\phi_1(u)\), and the unique continuous inverse-Fourier representatives give \(\sum_xp_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\). Consistency and weak unconfoundedness give equality with \(\sum_xp_xm_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)\) almost everywhere; target positivity and continuity of both sides promote the equality pointwise, so this expression equals the causal target \(\mu(a)=E_P[Y(a)]\) on \(\mathcal I\). If additionally \(U_1=U_2=0\), it reduces to the ordinary finite-stratum g-formula. This dependent, non-root proposition is solely a fidelity check and makes no novelty claim.
statements.justification: This already-known, non-root reduction checks that the analytic cocycle changes only the measurement-error inversion and preserves the established causal target.
statements.gap: No research gap is claimed for this proposition: HuangZhang2023 establishes the known-error deconvolution benchmark, which is retained only to verify that the blind functional targets the same ADRF.
statements.consumer: The reduction permits validation against conventional known-error analyses and direct comparison with an error-free generalized-propensity analysis.

statements.statement: For each \(\lambda=\lambda_{\gamma,L}\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}\), let \(\mathcal M(\lambda)=\{P\in\mathcal M:\underline\varphi_P(T)\ge\lambda(T)\ \forall T\ge\nu\}\) be the declared nested operator-strength subclass. Determine whether the empirical spectral-envelope handle yields one band \(\mathcal B_n^{\mathrm{ad}}\) that is honest over \(\mathcal M\) and, simultaneously for each \(\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}\), satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(\lambda)}E_P[W(\mathcal B_n^{\mathrm{ad}})]\le C\max\{w_n^{\star}(\lambda),s_n^{\star}(\lambda)\}\). Establish whether the candidate frontier \(s_n^{\star}(\lambda)=\inf\{w>0:\Delta_n(\lambda,w)\ge1-2\alpha\}\) is necessary and sufficient, or identify the correct testing-separation functional and the resulting Low-type impossibility boundary.
statements.justification: The broad class forces logarithmic width, but real replicate errors may be much better behaved; the honest adaptation frontier is the first-class open content beyond the matched fixed-class result.
statements.gap: CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 adapts point estimation to a tail parameter and discusses noise regularity, KatoSasaki2019 studies bands under a fixed polynomial ordinary-smooth operator condition, and Low1997 limits confidence-set adaptation; none characterizes adaptation across the newly indexed blind lower-envelope subclasses for an ADRF band.
statements.consumer: A positive frontier would let the same nutrition-analysis workflow remain protected against spectral zeros while automatically producing narrower bands when the recall errors are empirically well conditioned.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed quantitative law \(P\in\mathcal M\), with consistency, weak unconfoundedness, and a continuous stratum potential-mean version on \(\mathcal I\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{1i},S_{2i})\), with finite-stratum \(X_i\), bounded \(Y_i\), and latent \(A_i\in[-R,R]\).
sampling_model.treatment: The continuous treatment \(A_i\) is latent and is observed only through \(S_{1i}=A_i+U_{1i}\) and \(S_{2i}=A_i+U_{2i}\).
sampling_model.overlap: For every stratum, \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) on the fixed target interval \(\mathcal I\), and \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance tuple \((p,\{f_x,q_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X_0},\phi_1,\phi_2)\) is jointly profiled using an explicit simultaneous multinomial region for \(p\) and inversion of coupled empirical characteristic-function restrictions over a compact-support analytic sieve of degree \(m_n\). Candidate \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) are evaluated through their unique continuous \(H^{\beta}\) representatives when the observed canonical ratio is projected. Consistency, weak unconfoundedness, positivity, and the separately maintained continuity of \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}\) establish that this ratio equals the causal target pointwise; potential-mean continuity is not used by the analytic inversion. The transform part uses a joint multiplier critical value on positive-variance nondeterministic coordinates and empirical-Bernstein additive radii on zero-variance coordinates; undersampled strata invoke the full-band default.

estimand_functional: \(F_x(s,t)=\mathcal Ff_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t),\quad G_x(s,t)=\mathcal Fq_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t),\quad \sum_xp_xm_x^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=\sum_xp_xq_x(a)/f_x(a),\quad \mathcal B_n(a)=\begin{cases}[\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_0}p_{\vartheta x}q_{\vartheta x}(a)/f_{\vartheta x}(a),\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_0}p_{\vartheta x}q_{\vartheta x}(a)/f_{\vartheta x}(a)],&\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\ne\varnothing,\ \min_x n_x\ge2,\\ {}[-1,1],&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\quad W(\mathcal B_n)\asymp r_n,\quad f_{\vartheta x},q_{\vartheta x}\text{ are evaluated through their unique continuous }H^{\beta}\text{ representatives}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies the latent signal and independent error laws up to translation over its H2 exponential-moment and tail-law class, while Theorems 2 and 4 give the relevant upper and lower rate results on pp. 4141--4173.
The paper's projected confidence band has uniform asymptotic size control and fixed-alternative consistency for a latent density without completeness.
Theorem 2 proves multiplier-bootstrap validity for an EIV regression band under ordinary-smooth conventional deconvolution.
Sections 2--3 on pp. 474--496 identify a continuous-treatment ADRF through known-error deconvolution and a weighted conditional expectation.
Theorem 1 and the matching upper results establish minimax sup-norm density-deconvolution rates for a known error law over smoothness classes.
The paper gives an inequality lower-bounding expected confidence-interval length from uniform coverage and testing affinity.
The paper extends Kotlarski identification to isolated zeros or to broader zeros under exponential-tail restrictions.

Under Assumptions A1--A3, Lemma 2.1 and equations (1)--(2) on pp. 140--142 identify latent and error densities from two independent indicators when the latent and error characteristic functions are nonvanishing everywhere; equations (5)--(8) and Theorems 3.1--3.4 on pp. 142--151 give empirical-characteristic-function estimators and uniform rates in four ordinary- and supersmooth cases.

Under Assumptions 1--3 and global nonvanishing of the observed transform, Theorem 1 and equations (11)--(16) on pp. 1049--1051 identify the smoothed nonparametric regression ratio by recovering Fourier numerator and denominator components from two measurements; Theorems 2--3 on pp. 1059--1063 give pointwise rates and asymptotic normality under the paper's additional regularity conditions.

Sections 2--3 and Theorems 3.1 and 3.5 show that repeated-measurement kernel estimators of a density and an errors-in-variables regression can be first-order equivalent to their known-error counterparts under a common independent replicate-error law with real-valued nowhere-zero characteristic function, quantitative ordinary- or supersmooth bounds, and the stated relative-smoothness conditions.

tldr: Unknown-error repeated-measurement regression, replicate-based recovery of error laws, and deconvolution of regression numerators and denominators are established results and are not claimed as contributions. The first contribution is joint analytic identification, on a compact-support submodel, of the latent density and a distinct observed signed outcome channel when the two blind error laws may be nonidentical and asymmetric and their characteristic functions may vanish on open frequency sets. A local observable ratio and analytic continuation recover unique continuous Sobolev representatives; consistency, weak unconfoundedness, positivity, and potential-mean continuity then identify the causal ADRF pointwise on \(\mathcal I\). The second contribution is a uniformly honest simultaneous causal ADRF band from joint inversion of stratum masses and both transform channels, with width \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\), a negligible root-\(n\) multinomial term, and explicit empty-stratum and zero-variance conventions. The third is a matching all-honest expected-width converse on a nonempty all-strata homogeneous Legendre--Bernoulli subclass that fixes the entire noisy-treatment marginal and leaves the marginal ADRF separation unattenuated. Continuity and \(\phi_r(0)=1\) guarantee a positive low-frequency modulus separately for each error law; the fixed common \(\nu\) and \(c_{\phi}\) used uniformly over the class are a maintained quantitative strength restriction, not a borrowed theorem or a novelty claim.

project_justification.gap: LiVuong1998 identifies and estimates unknown latent and error densities from repeated indicators under global nonvanishing, Schennach2004 identifies and estimates a repeated-measurement nonparametric regression numerator and denominator under a global nonvanishing observed transform, and DelaigleHallMeister2008 proves first-order equivalence between unknown- and known-error density and regression point estimators under a common real-valued nowhere-zero error transform. Those foundational tasks are not novel here. The unresolved gap is simultaneous causal inference when the two blind errors are nonidentical and asymmetric and may have open spectral zero sets: no cited result jointly identifies the compact-support signed outcome channel in that regime, constructs a uniformly honest ADRF band, and proves a matching all-honest expected-width converse while holding the noisy-treatment marginal fixed.
project_justification.niche: Compact treatment support makes the latent density and signed outcome-weighted measure analytic objects, allowing local information to cross open spectral gaps without assuming an invertible deconvolution operator. Finite-stratum confounding adjustment keeps analytic recovery of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) separate from the causal continuity bridge between \(q_x/f_x\) and \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}\). Smoothness of \(q_x\) is primitive observed-channel response regularity, while continuity of \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}\) is a distinct mild but untestable continuous-dose causal condition. For any single error law, continuity and \(\phi_r(0)=1\) supply a law-specific positive neighborhood; common fixed \(\nu\) and \(c_{\phi}\) across all laws are maintained to make the class quantitatively uniform, without restricting open zeros away from that neighborhood.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies exactly three root contributions: joint analytic identification of \(f_x\) and the signed \(q_x\) under blind nonidentical asymmetric open-zero errors, with pointwise ADRF recovery through the declared causal bridge; a total coupled inversion yielding a uniformly honest simultaneous causal band; and a matched all-honest expected-width converse from a quantitatively compatible all-strata homogeneous Bernoulli hard family. The confidence set jointly covers multinomial stratum masses and both empirical transform channels, while the fixed \(p^{\star}\), common \(f_0\), fixed errors, and identical smooth outcome perturbation keep the lower-bound noisy-treatment marginal fixed and the ADRF separation unattenuated.

related_work: LiVuong1998 is the foundational unknown-error multiple-indicator density paper. Its model on pp. 139--141 has \(Y_j=X+\varepsilon_j\), initially with mutually independent \(X,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\), identically distributed mean-zero errors, and latent and error characteristic functions nonvanishing everywhere; the discussion on p. 142 notes that Kotlarski identification itself permits nonidentical errors while retaining mutual independence. Lemma 2.1 and equations (1)--(2) on p. 141 identify the latent and error densities; equations (5)--(8) on pp. 142--143 construct their empirical-characteristic-function estimators. For rates, A4--A5 on pp. 145--146 require bounded supports and integrable characteristic functions, Theorems 3.1--3.4 on pp. 147--151 cover the four ordinary- and supersmooth cases, and Lemma 4.1 on pp. 154--155 controls inversion on expanding frequency sets. Replicate-based error-law recovery and unknown-error density deconvolution are therefore explicitly non-novel here. Schennach2004 is the foundational unknown-error repeated-measurement regression comparator. Equations (7)--(8) on p. 1049 observe \(x=x^*+\Delta_x\) and \(z=x^*+\Delta_z\); Assumption 1 imposes conditional mean restrictions on the outcome and first-measurement errors and independence of \(\Delta_z\) from \(x^*\), while Assumptions 2--3 impose integrability. Theorem 1 and equations (11)--(16) on pp. 1049--1051 identify the smoothed Nadaraya--Watson numerator and denominator from observable Fourier moments provided \(|E[e^{i\xi z}]|>0\) at every finite frequency. Assumption 4 on p. 1051 compactly supports the kernel transform; Assumption 8 and equations (39)--(41) on pp. 1056--1057 impose Fourier tail bounds and a global lower modulus for the observed transform; Theorem 2 on pp. 1059--1061 derives pointwise rates, and Theorem 3 on p. 1063 gives asymptotic normality under further regularity. Unknown-error repeated-measurement regression and numerator--denominator recovery are accordingly non-novel; the separation is the present open-zero analytic continuation, coupled honest causal band, and all-honest converse. DelaigleHallMeister2008, equations (2.1)--(2.6) on pp. 668--670, treats density and regression deconvolution under a common identically distributed replicate-error law totally independent of the signal and regression error; condition (2.2) on p. 668 requires its characteristic function to be real-valued and nowhere zero. Theorems 3.1 and 3.5 on pp. 670--676 use bounded replicate counts, enough replicate pairs, a compactly supported kernel transform, two-sided ordinary-smooth bound (3.1), and relative smoothness condition (3.12) to prove first-order equivalence with known-error density and regression estimators; Section 3.7 on p. 676 gives the supersmooth analogue. That first-order-equivalence result is also non-novel here. CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025, Theorem 1 on pp. 4141--4173, proves latent-signal and error-law identification over a broader H2 exponential-moment/tail class, and Theorems 2 and 4 give the relevant rate comparison. The present compact-support identification adds a shared signed outcome channel and pointwise causal bridge without extending their latent-law class. Continuity and \(\phi_r(0)=1\) give each distribution its own positive local modulus, but the shared constants \(\nu\) and \(c_{\phi}\) over \(\mathcal M\) are a maintained uniform-strength class restriction; they are not attributed to Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehericy and do not exclude open zeros outside the local neighborhood. KatoSasakiUra2021 supplies robust complex-moment inversion but only a latent-density band without a sharp ADRF width. KatoSasaki2019 supplies simultaneous EIV regression process tools under an invertible ordinary-smooth operator and is method precedent, not a result claimed to be strengthened. HuangZhang2023, Sections 2--3 on pp. 474--496, supplies the known-error causal ADRF functional retained only as an already-known non-root benchmark. Potential-mean continuity is separately maintained here to promote causal equality to every dose; it neither aids analytic recovery nor changes the rate. LouniciNickl2011 supplies known-operator sup-norm packing geometry, Low1997 supplies the coverage-to-expected-width inequality, and EvdokimovWhite2012 treats Kotlarski zeros under different zero or tail restrictions. Schennach2016 is survey context only.
technical_internal_limitation: The sharp lower bound depends on proving that the mollified Legendre direction simultaneously retains \(H^{\beta}\)-boundedness, representative-level sup-norm separation \(m^{1/2-\beta}\), Bernoulli feasibility, and superexponentially small image under the fixed compact-spectrum two-replicate operator. The homogeneous replication of this direction over all strata must factor the observed experiment as an ancillary \(p^{\star}\) component times the same outcome-channel experiment, so neither the separation nor total variation changes. Failure of any one of these properties changes the claimed minimax width and is the prescribed early kill test.

This is a genuine untestable but mild continuous-dose causal regularity condition; it is not implied by smoothness of \(q_x\), does not help analytic recovery, and does not change the rate. Consistency and weak unconfoundedness identify \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}=q_x/f_x\) only almost everywhere, while target positivity and continuity of both sides promote equality to every \(a\in\mathcal I\). Every projected endpoint, coverage event, and lower-bound separation uses these same versions, and the smooth Legendre--Bernoulli hard family satisfies the causal continuity condition. The fixed constants obey the necessary nonemptiness coherence \(|\mathcal X_0|p_{\min}\le1\), making the uniform vector \(p_x^{\star}=|\mathcal X_0|^{-1}\) admissible. The hard family is homogeneous on the full declared \(\mathcal X_0\): every stratum has \(A\mid X=x\sim f_0\), the same admissible errors, and the same smooth Bernoulli mean \(1/2\pm v_m/f_0\). Covariates are restricted to finitely many strata, all quantitative radii are fixed, and the target interval stays inside a uniform positive-density region. The band jointly projects candidate stratum masses from a simultaneous multinomial region, whose root-\(n\) diameter is negligible relative to \(r_n\). It is defined as \([-1,1]\) on undersampled strata or empty inversion sets, and zero empirical variances use the declared additive radius. Adaptation over \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and the exact separation frontier are open. The known nonvanishing-error reduction is the already-known Huang--Zhang sanity benchmark, is a dependent non-root proposition excluded from the research theorem count, and with no measurement error reduces further to the finite-stratum g-formula.

LiVuong1998, Assumptions A1--A3, Lemma 2.1, and equations (1)--(8) on pp. 140--143, already identifies and estimates latent and error densities from repeated indicators under global nonvanishing; Theorems 3.1--3.4 on pp. 147--151 already give uniform rates. DelaigleHallMeister2008, equations (2.1)--(2.6), condition (2.2), and Theorems 3.1 and 3.5 on pp. 668--676, already recovers density and regression point estimators from a common replicate-error law and proves first-order equivalence to known-error procedures under its real-valued nowhere-zero ordinary- or supersmooth operator conditions. Thus unknown-error repeated-measurement regression, replicate-based error-law recovery, regression numerator--denominator deconvolution, and nonvanishing ordinary- or supersmooth regression estimation are not contributions of this project. The first novelty claim is joint analytic identification of the compact-support latent density and shared signed outcome-weighted channel under blind nonidentical asymmetric errors whose characteristic functions may have open zero sets, with recovery of their continuous Sobolev representatives and pointwise causal ADRF recovery through the declared continuity bridge. CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025, Theorem 1 on pp. 4141--4173, recovers a latent probability law and error laws over a broader H2 exponential-moment/tail class; the present local \(G_x/F_x\) transfer, signed-measure continuation, and stable division add the shared outcome channel only on its compact-support submodel and do not extend its latent-law class. The fixed common local-modulus constants are a maintained quantitative class restriction: continuity and \(\phi_r(0)=1\) provide only distribution-specific constants, and CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 is not invoked as support for uniform \(\nu\) and \(c_{\phi}\). This restriction is not counted as a novelty claim.
